newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU says concerned at attack on Burma's Suu Kyi.
newsitem.headline: EU says concerned at attack on Burma's Suu Kyi.

text.p: European Union president Ireland said on Friday it was deeply concerned by the aggression committed against Aung San Suu Kyi and other leaders of Burma's National League for Democracy (NLD) on November 9.

"The EU holds the State Law and Order Restoration Council responsible for safeguarding the security of the NLD leaders and considers that these incidents mark a clear deterioration in the political situation," Ireland said in a statement on behalf of the 15-nation bloc.

The EU called for a full and thorough investigation and explanation of what happened and appealed to Burma's military government to exercise maximum restraint and to guarantee safety, liberty and free expression to all those undertaking normal political activities in support of democracy.
"The EU will monitor the situation very carefully to watch for any repetition of such acts which would be bound to inflict further damage to Myanmar's international standing," it said.
It called on the Burmese government to engage without delay in a meaningful dialogue with members of the democratic movement as the only way to achieve national reconciliation.
Suu Kyi, who emerged uninjured from last weekend's attack on her car and other vehicles travelling in her convoy, has accused the government of orchestrating the incident.
Officials have denied involvement and said on Friday that the government has launched an investigation into the attack.
